reran: cmd.sh on w4-int, w3-int, w3-base and 2.13.18: identical to actual.txt (default compiles, -Ydelambdafy:inline gives the AbstractFunction0[C] with Serializable mismatch). Older releases with -Ydelambdafy:inline: 2.11.12 compiles; 2.12.4, 2.12.8, 2.12.15, 2.13.0, 2.13.5 and 2.13.10 reject (2.12.0 to 2.12.3 not run, they need JDK 8). run/existentials3-new and -old fail under the flag on w4-int. Under the default -Ydelambdafy:method the same error comes from a lambda in a super-constructor argument or an early definition (class Q extends P(() => E6.f), with def f = { trait A; class K extends A; class C extends K; new C }) on w4-int, w3-base and 2.13.18; Scala 3.7.4 compiles and runs that program.
user_impact: -Ydelambdafy:inline is not only legacy: mdoc sets it for every Scala 2 compile (scala/bug#9824) and Scastie adds it to every 2.12 and 2.13 snippet (scala/bug#10782), and the ZIO ecosystem build helper sets it in console settings. Without the flag, any lambda in a super-constructor argument or early definition is expanded the same way. The trigger is a lambda whose result type is an inferred existential with a bound that names another quantifier, which comes from returning a local class whose hierarchy has a class between it and a local trait, e.g. def mk = { trait Shape; abstract class Base extends Shape; class Circle extends Base; List(new Circle) } and then () => mk.head. Uncommon, but ordinary-looking code.
fixability: clear cut: in TreeGen.expandFunction build the AbstractFunctionN parent from the function type's arguments (fun.tpe.typeArgs) when fun.tpe is a FunctionN type, as 2.11 did, instead of from fun.body.tpe, which is the existential skolem; no binary or behaviour cost beyond the anonymous class's generic signature naming the packed type.
regression: from 2.12: 2.11.12 compiles it; 2.12.0's SAM refactoring (ad90614c39, then 7025be9a46 'Bring back AbstractFunction parent', both in v2.12.0) changed the parent from abstractFunctionForFunctionType(fun.tpe) to abstractFunctionType(..., fun.body.tpe.deconst).
links: scala/bug#10564 is another -Ydelambdafy:inline-only compiler failure (private extension method, crash), a different cause. Wave-two FO1, FT3, PV5 (retronym/scala PR 436) are -Ydelambdafy:inline VerifyErrors from lifted try blocks, a different cause. No duplicate among wave-four findings.
note: Mechanism, checked with a probe on w4-int: typer gives `() => f` the packed type Function0[C forSome { type C <: AnyRef with A; type A <: AnyRef }] while the body's type is an existential skolem C' whose bound is AnyRef with A' (A' another skolem). UnCurry's expandFunction makes the anonymous class extend AbstractFunction0[C'] and re-types Typed(New(anon), TypeTree(fun.tpe)); C' <:< C forSome {...} is already false at typer (explaintypes shows both quantifiers solved to Nothing: A occurs only in C's bound, so the solver never learns A := A'). This is a weakness of existential subtyping with dependent quantifier bounds that the expansion exposes; the expansion should not re-check what typer packed. The hunter's fix sketch (skolemise or skip the check) works too, but taking the parent from fun.tpe is the smaller change and restores 2.11. The hunter understated reach: the default delambdafy strategy is affected in constructor arguments, and two widely used tools set the flag. A hand-written existential of the same shape compiles, because typer simplifies it; the dependent bound only survives packing of local classes.
